column1: # security group, build A (note 0009 D7.1, B11). Builder A (Claude Sonnet), 2026-11-20.
# Sources: EasyMesh through the usp-spec MCP server (doc easymesh): section 3.1.2 Conventions, 17.2.54 Table 76, 17.2.55 Table 77, 17.2.56
#   Table 103, 17.2.82 Table 104, 17.2.83 Table 105, 17.2.86 Table 108. TLV codes from the tables match em-types codes.rs:302, 304, 305,
#   (chirp receiver), :328-366 (chirp sender: 2-octet hash length written at :356-358), :368-413 (encap DPP receiver), :415-449 (encap DPP
#   sender: flag octet, MAC if dest_mac, frame type, 2-octet network-order length :446), em_provisioning.cpp:51-73 (CCE sender), :318-351
#   (DPP Message sender), em.cpp:1157-1254 (AKM sender: back count, back suites, front count, front suites), em_base.h:1011-1020,
#   241-243 (0xcd), 244 (0xce), 245 (0xcf), 246 (0xd2), 247-251 (0xd3), 257-258 (0xd1). port_rule SPEC or "-" on every row; no UPSTREAM
#   rows, so no little-endian host-order field in this group.
#   Note 0009: D2 (raw reserved values, zero counts where a count may be 0), D4 (strict decoder = spec; lenient only for a production
#   sender's non-spec form), D5 (frames, URIs, MIC, encrypted payloads, tunneled frames and EAPOL are raw bytes; the Chirp hash length is
#   1 octet, intentional difference from upstream's 2), D6 (no host-order field here), D8 (zero counts invalid only where "one or more":
#   no such count in this group), A8 (a "shall" rule that governs presence is ValueOutOfRange: none applies, see Choices).
# Byte order of every multi-octet integer (hex = tlvValue only):
#   0xab Integrity Transmission Counter (6 octets): BIG-endian 48-bit integer; spec says "Variable" with no order, so section 3.1.2 (the
#     1905.1 conventions: network order); audit 214 (SPEC, no upstream code). Item `counter`, written as a 0x-hex or decimal integer.
#   0xab MIC Length (2): big-endian; spec table (2 octets) + section 3.1.2; audit 214.
#   0xac Encryption Transmission Counter (6): big-endian 48-bit integer; section 3.1.2; audit 215 (SPEC, no upstream code).
#   0xcd Encapsulated frame length (2): big-endian; section 3.1.2 and audit 241 (upstream writes it with set_net_uint16_from_host,
#   0xd3 Hash Length: ONE octet (spec Table 105; audit 247 SPEC; upstream's 2-octet field is the intentional difference, note 0008 D8).
#   Raw octet strings with NO byte order applied: 0xcc BH/FH OUI (3 octets, copied as written, the 802.11 AKM selector order), the
#     frames, URIs, MIC, AES-SIV and EAPOL payloads (note 0009 D5).
#   Every other field is a 1-octet integer, a count, a 6-octet MAC (RUID, BSSID, bSTA address, AL MAC, STA MAC) or a bit-field octet.
# Wire layouts (tlvValue only; ranges are spec table rows):
#   0xc1 Tunneled Message Type: Type(1): 0 Assoc Req, 1 Re-Assoc Req, 2 BTM Query, 3 WNM Request, 4 ANQP req for Neighbor Report,
#        5 DSCP Policy Query, 6 DSCP Policy Response, 7-0xff reserved (raw). Fixed 1 octet.
#   0xc2 Tunneled: Body(n), the 802.11 request frame body, raw octets. The spec gives no minimum: n may be 0.
#   0xa9 1905 Layer Security Capability: Onboarding Protocol(1; 0 = 1905 Device Provisioning Protocol, 1-0xff reserved), MIC
#        Algorithm(1; 0 = HMAC-SHA256, 1-0xff reserved), Encryption Algorithm(1; 0 = AES-SIV, 1-0xff reserved). Fixed 3 octets.
#   0xab MIC: octet {1905 GTK Key Id b7-6 (2-bit value 0-3), MIC Version b5-4 (2-bit value; 0 = version 1, 1-3 reserved, carried raw),
#        Reserved b3-0}, Integrity Transmission Counter(6), Source 1905 AL MAC Address(6), MIC Length(2) = n, MIC(n octets, raw).
#        tlvLength = 15 + n. The MIC is raw octets (D5); n = 0 is allowed (spec gives no minimum).
#   0xac Encrypted Payload: Encryption Transmission Counter(6), Source 1905 AL MAC Address(6), Destination 1905 AL MAC Address(6),
#        AES-SIV length(2) = n, AES-SIV(n octets, raw: SIV concatenated with the encrypted TLVs). n = 0 is allowed.
#   0xcc AKM Suite Capabilities: Num_BackAKM(1), Num_BackAKM x { BH OUI(3), BH AKM Suite Type(1) }, Num_FrontAKM(1),
#        Num_FrontAKM x { FH OUI(3), FH AKM Suite Type(1) }. Both counts may be 0 (the spec says "Variable"; no "one or more").
#   0xcd 1905 Encap DPP: octet {Enrollee MAC Address Present b7, Reserved b6, DPP Frame Indicator b5 (0 = DPP Public Action frame,
#        1 = GAS frame), Reserved b4-0}, Destination STA MAC Address(6; present ONLY if bit 7 = 1), Frame Type(1), Encapsulated frame
#        length(2) = n, Encapsulated frame(n octets, raw). Frame Type is "set to" the DPP Public Action frame type when bit 5 = 0 and
#        "set to 255" otherwise; the codec carries the octet raw (not a "shall" rule on presence, A8). n = 0 is allowed.
#   0xce 1905 Encap EAPOL: EAPOL frame payload(n octets, raw). The spec gives no minimum: n may be 0.
#   0xcf DPP Bootstrapping URI Notification: RUID(6), BSSID(6), bSTA Address(6), DPP URI(n octets, raw; no terminator stated). n may be 0.
#   0xd2 DPP CCE Indication: Advertise CCE(1): 1 = Enable, 0 = Disable; 2-0xff are carried raw (the codec does not decide policy).
#        Fixed 1 octet. (The table's tlvLength 1 is the value length.)
#   0xd3 DPP Chirp Value: octet {Enrollee MAC Address Present b7, Hash Validity b6 (1 = establish, 0 = purge), Reserved b5-0},
#        Destination STA MAC Address(6; present ONLY if bit 7 = 1), Hash Length(1) = k, Hash Value(k octets, raw). Hash Length and Hash
#        Value are present whatever Hash Validity says. k = 0 is allowed (the spec gives no minimum). (The table's tlvLength "1" is a
#        stray; the TLV is variable length.)
#   0xd1 DPP Message: DPP Frame(n octets, raw: the DPP frame as defined in the Wi-Fi Easy Connect specification). n may be 0.
# Group field-reading rules (how `fields` determines the bytes; used by both builders):
#   (1) Items are written in the listed order, each at its own position, except the bit-group item of rule (3).
#   (2) Item names. 0xc0 sta_mac. 0xc1 msg_type. 0xc2 body. 0xa9 onboarding, mic_alg, enc_alg. 0xab gtk_key_id, mic_version, flags_rsv,
#       counter, src_mac, mic_len, mic. 0xac counter, src_mac, dst_mac, siv_len, siv. 0xcc back (the count Num_BackAKM), bh<i>_oui,
#       bh<i>_type (entry i), front (Num_FrontAKM), fh<i>_oui, fh<i>_type. 0xcd mac_present, frame_indicator, flags_rsv, dest_mac,
#       frame_type, frame_len, frame. 0xce eapol. 0xcf ruid, bssid, bsta_mac, uri. 0xd2 advertise. 0xd3 mac_present, hash_valid,
#       flags_rsv, dest_mac, hash_len, hash. 0xd1 frame. Counts and length items (back, front, mic_len, siv_len, frame_len, hash_len)
#       are written exactly as given and are NOT derived from the data items that follow: a count or length above the data listed is an
#       overstated count or length. Only the entries listed follow.
#   (3) Bit-field octets: each group is ONE octet, written at the position of the group's first listed item; flag values are 0/1
#       unshifted; a 2-bit value (0xab gtk_key_id and mic_version) is 0-3 unshifted, placed at its bit range; a reserved mask
#       (flags_rsv) is given in octet position and ORed in (absent = 0). A group none of whose items is listed is absent from the bytes.
#       Groups: 0xab {gtk_key_id b7-6, mic_version b5-4, flags_rsv b3-0}; 0xcd {mac_present b7, frame_indicator b5, flags_rsv = bits 6 and
#       4-0, so a mask within 0x5f}; 0xd3 {mac_present b7, hash_valid b6, flags_rsv b5-0}. A case that sets a reserved mask: the decoder
#       ignores it, the encoder writes zero (the canonical bytes are those of the sibling case with the same fields and flags_rsv=0: `reserved-bits-clear`
#   (4) Widths: 6-octet MACs (12 lowercase hex digits): sta_mac, src_mac, dst_mac, dest_mac, ruid, bssid, bsta_mac. 6-octet big-endian
#       integers: counter (0x-hex or decimal). 2-octet big-endian integers: mic_len, siv_len, frame_len. 1-octet integers: msg_type,
#       onboarding, mic_alg, enc_alg, back, front, bh<i>_type, fh<i>_type, frame_type, hash_len, advertise. Values are decimal or 0x-hex.
#   (5) Byte-string items are hex: raw octets written exactly as given, with NO length octet in front: body, mic, siv, frame, eapol, uri,
#       hash, bh<i>_oui and fh<i>_oui (3 octets each). `hex:` alone is no octets.
#   (6) An item given as hex: where it normally takes a MAC, an integer or an OUI is a cut field: exactly those raw octets are written
#       (an empty hex: writes nothing for that item), and nothing after it is written. An item not listed ends the bytes there.
#       A row with no data items (only kind and error) is the empty value.
#   (7) trailing=hex: raw octets appended after everything listed (even after a cut field). `kind=` and `error=` items (kind=invalid with
#       error=Truncated|TrailingBytes) are not data: they write no octets; a builder copies them and derives only the hex.
#   (8) Presence rule: dest_mac (0xcd, 0xd3) is written only when listed; a row lists it exactly when the mac_present bit is 1 (except
#       the cut and missing-field invalid rows, which say so by their names).
# Choices (for the coordinator): (a) Every cut field, partial entry or overstated count/length is error=Truncated; octets after a complete
#   fixed layout are TrailingBytes (including after zero counts, zero lengths and zero-count AKM lists). 0xc2, 0xce, 0xd1 (raw bodies) and
#   0xcf (raw URI at the end) have no trailing case: every octet after the fixed part is the body. (b) Empty raw payloads are valid spec
#   rows: 0xc2 body, 0xce EAPOL payload, 0xd1 DPP frame, 0xcf URI, 0xab mic_len 0, 0xac siv_len 0, 0xcd frame_len 0, 0xd3 hash_len 0. The
#   spec says "Variable" or "n octets" with no minimum and never "one or more" (D8), and D5 says the codec carries these bytes raw. Upstream
#   rejects a zero-length EAPOL TLV on receive (audit 244) and a zero Hash Length when Hash Validity is 1 (ec_util.cpp:302-307); both are
#   policy for the consumer, not wire rules. Alternative: make those rows invalid (ValueOutOfRange or Truncated). (c) 0xd3: Hash Length and
#   Hash Value are present whatever Hash Validity says (spec Table 105 rows 5-6, audit 248 SPEC): a purge case carries a hash, and a value
#   that ends after the flags octet (and MAC) is invalid Truncated, even for a purge (purge-flags-only). Upstream's sender omits both for
#   hash_validity false but no caller does that (audit 248). (d) 0xd3 and 0xcd: dest_mac is present exactly when mac_present is 1 (layout
#   rule, not an A8 rule); a case with the bit set and the MAC missing or cut is Truncated. A MAC listed with the bit clear is not modelled.
#   (e) 0xcd Frame Type: indicator 1 with a Frame Type other than 255, and indicator 0 with 255, are kind=spec rows (the spec says "is set
#   to"; it is a value the codec carries raw, D2, not a presence rule, A8). Reserved bits 6 and 4-0 are carried raw (reserved-* rows with
#   canonical siblings). (f) 0xc1 values 7-0xff, 0xa9 values 1-0xff of each field, 0xab MIC Version 1-3 and 0xd2 values 2-0xff are kind=spec,
#   carried raw (D2). The 0xd2 values 2-0xff are not listed in the spec table at all: carried raw, no ValueOutOfRange. (g) 0xab GTK Key Id has
#   no stated range: the 2-bit field takes 0-3 (all four are spec rows). (h) Byte orders the spec leaves open: 0xab and 0xac 6-octet counters
#   are 48-bit big-endian integers (3.1.2); the 2-octet MIC, AES-SIV and frame lengths are big-endian. The counter bytes could instead be
#   modelled as 6 raw octets with no order (the same bytes). (i) 0xcc: both counts may be 0 (zero-back, zero-front, zero-both); counts are
#   1 octet so up to 255 entries: back-255 and front-255 pin that there is no cap (upstream's receiver keeps 10 per BSS, a policy, audit 240;
#   eleven-back pins 11). OUI is 3 raw octets (oui-order is not byte-swapped); the AKM Suite Type is any value 0-255 (type 0xff row).
#   Duplicates are not rejected. (j) 0xc0 accepts any EUI-48 (broadcast, zero). (k) 0xcf URI: raw, no terminator rule; a trailing NUL octet is
#   kept (uri-with-nul). (l) Two rows record upstream's wrong Chirp bytes as invalid (upstream-2-octet-hash-length, -no-mac): the strict
#   decoder reads Hash Length 0 and finds the rest as TrailingBytes; this is the intentional-difference test for audit row 247.
# New lenient candidates (non-spec forms an upstream sender writes; not added): (1) 0xd3 DPP Chirp Value with a 2-octet big-endian Hash
#   Length: flags octet, [MAC 6], 0x00 k, hash (k octets). Sender ec_util.cpp:337 (size sizeof(uint16_t) + hash_len) and :356-358
#   (set_net_uint16_from_host), called with a hash from ec_pa_configurator.cpp:54, ec_ctrl_configurator.cpp:178, :368 and
#   ec_enrollee.cpp:1863, and carried by em_provisioning.cpp:105, :296 and em_configuration.cpp:4467-4469, :4585. With a 32-octet hash the
#   value is 0x40 or 0xc0, [MAC], 0x00 0x20, hash. A strict decoder reads Hash Length 0 and TrailingBytes (rows upstream-2-octet-hash-length,
#   upstream-2-octet-hash-length-no-mac), so this form is not also a spec form (D4 rule satisfied). A lenient decoder could accept a value
#   whose octet after the flags (and MAC) is 0x00 and whose following octet equals the number of octets left, and normalise to the 1-octet
#   Hash Length. Ambiguity: none for k > 0 (a spec value with Hash Length 0 has no octets after it). (2) 0xd3 purge form without Hash Length
#   or Hash Value (flags octet [+ MAC] only, ec_util.cpp:337, :356-363): no production caller passes hash_validity false (audit 248), so
#   it is not proposed. The 0xcd, 0xcc, 0xd1, 0xd2 and 0xa9 senders write spec bytes (0xa9: data-model values, em_capability.cpp:206-208,
#   em_configuration.cpp:4436-4438, possibly reserved values: covered by the reserved rows). No sender writes 0xc0, 0xc1, 0xc2, 0xab, 0xac,
#   0xcf. (3) 0xcd sender sizes its buffer on dest_mac != NULL but sets the MAC-present bit the same way (ec_util.cpp:418, :432): no
#   mismatch, no extra form. 0xd3 sender sizes on dest_mac != NULL but writes the MAC on mac_present (:336, :352): no caller passes both
# Coordinator correction (2026-11-20, user decision before builder B): 0xd3 gets a lenient decoder for upstream's
#   2-octet big-endian Hash Length (ec_util.cpp:337, 356-358). The rows upstream-2-octet-hash-length and
#   kind=lenient;decoded=upstream-2-octet-hash-length (the strict decoder still rejects them). Bytes unchanged.
# Coordinator correction (2026-11-20, after comparing the builds): 0xcc back-overstated-front-count-present lists
#   front=0 after the single backhaul entry; its octet is written (02000fac08 -> 02000fac0800). Build A had stopped at
#   the overstated list, which made the row identical to back-overstated.
